questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
Relevance for my study
English speaking country
A place I where I had not been before

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Everything was so nice and well organized. Although I had a hard time getting used to a different system and the differences between the levels of the different units. Besides this the university was very helpful and the professors are really interested in making sure that everyone can follow the unit.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, although sometimes it took a long time before you got through or got any response.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had to change unit because I discovered after my first class that the unit was a follow up unit from a previous unit. Therefore I couldn’t follow the class. It took quite a while before the transfer to another unit got accepted so I almost missed two weeks of the new unit which gave me a lot of extra work in the end.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was not that easy because covid had made it both very expensive but also just difficult so find anything. I would recommend looking at Fairy Floss on facebook.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It might be very fare form the university but it's definitely worth it since the social life at campus is restricted and you cannot go to the central of Melbourne at night since the trains stop before midnight.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very expensive

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We arrived and checked in with our names which was nice and easy. Unfortunately I found it difficult to find the social activities and therefore missed a lot of them. There was a limit amount of people on each event so I was often too late.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: A lot of help. There were people provided especially for exchange student and also a big office for general help. Also the teachers and the teacher assistance were very helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesful although my professor in one of my units did not understand why I got accepted to his unit since I did not have the right knowledge to follow the classes.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do easy classes and look for the ones you just have to pass.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Some of the were very easy and I just had to pass while some of them were very difficult and you has to spend a lot of time fulfilling the tasks. I big difference was that you had to do something every week and everything you had to submit counted towards your final grade.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More week based program where everything you submit and everything you do in class count towards the final grade while in Denmark everything is based on the final exam.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Microbes in Health and Disease
Conservation Biology
Global change Biology
The Dynamic Cell - Molecular Cell Biology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Conservation Biology and The Dynamic Cell

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Live with some Australien housemates ! That's the best way to experience and understand Melbourne.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Rent a car and go on roadtrips. Their hips of pleases to visit and it's all so beautiful.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Live with local people.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That there were lots of different opportunities and everyone are friendly and wants to help you.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be prepared for the time you spend on going to the university.
Live with local people.
Just makes sure you pass the exams

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Enjoy it, times fly

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting a few but very close local friends

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The workload
